ikar_intro.title: Fire
ikar_intro.narrator: Ikar. Bearer of Fire. What he never says.
ikar_intro.text:
Fire doesn't lie.

It burns or it doesn't.

It's the only honest thing I know.

ikar_pourquoi_feu.title: Why Fire
ikar_pourquoi_feu.text:
People think fire is anger.

They're not wrong.

But it's something else too.

Clarity.

When everything burns,
there are no shadows left.
No place left to hide.

Truth or ashes.

I always preferred that to Aryn's nuance.
To Vael's humor.
To Taera's gentleness.

They navigate the grays.

Me, I need to know exactly where I'm putting my feet.

ikar_enfance_a.title: The Forge
ikar_enfance_a.text:
My father was a blacksmith.

His father before him.

I was supposed to be one too.

I loved it.
The heat.
The noise.
The metal that changes under your hands.

By five I was already in the forge.
By seven I was working the bellows.

My father said I had the hands for it.

He was right about the hands.
Wrong about the trade.

ikar_pere.title: The Father
ikar_pere.text:
Yes.

He worked hard.
He didn't talk much.

When he was pleased, he tapped the anvil twice.

That was his way of saying good.

The last time I heard that sound,
I was seven.

After that.

After that he never tapped the anvil again.

ikar_accident.title: The Accident
ikar_accident.text:
I was seven.

A spark from the forge.

Normal.

But this one landed on my hand.

And it didn't burn.

It grew.

I looked at my palm.

A flame.
Small.
Dancing on my skin without consuming it.

My father was behind me.

He saw.

He didn't tap the anvil.

ikar_reaction_pere.title: The Silence
ikar_reaction_pere.text:
He set his hammer down.

Slowly.

He looked at my hand.

Then he looked at the wall.

He stayed like that for a whole minute.

Then he said:

**"Put it out."**

**"I don't know how."**

**"Try."**

I tried.

It took three hours.

We didn't have dinner that night.
We didn't talk either.

The next morning he was back at the forge.
As if nothing had happened.

Except he had started wearing gloves.

ikar_peur_pere.title: The Gloves
ikar_peur_pere.text:
Yes.

I understood later.

He loved me.
But he was afraid.

Both at once.

I wanted to tell him I was scared too.

But we didn't talk much in that forge.

The gloves stayed on.

Until the day the Order came.

After they left, he took them off.

I don't know what that meant.

I still think about it sometimes.

ikar_controle_feu.title: Learning to Burn
ikar_controle_feu.text:
I taught myself.

No choice.

My father didn't want anyone to know.
The village wasn't big.

Every morning before dawn.
Out in the fields.

The first few weeks I burned a lot of grass.

Then I figured something out.

Fire follows intention.

If I think about destroying, it destroys.
If I think about warming, it warms.
If I think about nothing, it goes wild.

Fire doesn't like an empty head.

So I learned never to think about nothing.

ikar_change.title: What It Does to You
ikar_change.text:
Always having something burning in your head.

It wears you down.

But it also teaches you to decide fast.

No time to hesitate.
No time for nuance.

Fire or no fire.
Yes or no.
Forward or back.

Aryn says I see everything in black and white.

She's right.

What she doesn't get
is that black and white
prevents a lot of mistakes.

ikar_recrutement.title: The Man in Red
ikar_recrutement.text:
He showed up one morning.

A man.
Old.
Dressed in red and orange.

He stopped in front of the forge.

He watched me work.

**"How long have you been doing this?"**

**"Learning to control it?"**

**"Yes."**

**"Three months."**

He nodded.

**"Come with me."**

**"Why?"**

**"Because you learned in three months**
**what most people take three years to understand."**

It was the first time someone told me
I was good at something
my father couldn't do.

ikar_depart_pere.title: The Departure
ikar_depart_pere.text:
My father was in the forge.

The man in red spoke to him.

My father listened.
He didn't ask any questions.

At the end he looked at me.

**"You want to go?"**

**"Yes."**

He nodded.

He went back to his anvil.

He didn't tap it twice.

But he didn't say no either.

That was his way of agreeing.

ikar_oui_immediat.title: Yes
ikar_oui_immediat.text:
Before he even finished his sentence.

Yes.

The man in red looked surprised.

**"You don't want to think it over?"**

**"No."**

Aryn always says I decide too fast.

Maybe.

But that decision was easy.

Staying in a forge where my father wore gloves.

Or going off to learn to be what I was.

Not hard.

ikar_aurenthal.title: Aurenthal
ikar_aurenthal.text:
Aurenthal didn't impress me.

Too big.
Too loud.
Too many people staring at each other.

The Temple of the Order was better.

Simple.
Tall.
Silent.

Three other kids were waiting.

A girl with silver hair.
She was staring at her hands.

A girl who smelled of earth.
She smiled at everyone.

A boy who watched everything at once.
He waved at me.

I didn't do anything.

The silver-haired girl looked up.

**"You're late."** I said.

**"I just came from the coast."**

**"Everyone comes from somewhere."**

Rough start.

We got past it eventually.

choices.text: What was it like with Aryn at first?

ikar_aryn_debut.title: Aryn — The Early Days
ikar_aryn_debut.text:
We argued all the time.

Not meanly.

She thought too much.
I acted too fast.

One night in training I said:

**"You spend more time doubting than doing."**

**"And you spend more time doing than thinking."**
**"Result?"**

**"I succeed."**

**"And you keep making the same mistakes."**

I didn't answer.

Because she was right.

We balanced each other out.
It took a while to admit it.

Now I admit it without any trouble.

She thinks for me.
I act for her.

It's a good balance.

ikar_entrainement.title: Training
ikar_entrainement.location: Temple of the Order — Fire Hall
ikar_entrainement.text:
The Spirit of Fire was called Kael.

Not Caël with the accent.
Kael. Different.

He'd been there since the Order was founded.

He didn't like questions.
Neither did I.

We got along well.

**"Fire doesn't forgive weakness."** he'd say.
**"A flame that hesitates goes out."**
**"A bearer who hesitates fails."**

Simple.
Direct.

I loved that.

Kael never said *maybe.*
He never said *it depends.*

Fire or no fire.

ikar_autres_esprits.title: The Other Spirits
ikar_autres_esprits.text:
The Spirit of Water spoke in metaphors.

Lyra.
She'd say things like:
*"Water always finds its way."*

I'd hear that and think:
*so what?*

The Spirit of Earth was gentle.
Too gentle for me.

The Spirit of Air was unsettling.

It would vanish in the middle of a sentence.
And come back somewhere else.

Vael loved that.

It drove me crazy.

Kael was different.

He said what he thought.
And he expected us to do the same.

We understood each other.

choices.text: Did Kael talk to you about them?

ikar_pret_a_tout.title: Ready for Anything
ikar_pret_a_tout.text:
I was ten.

Kael kept me back after training.

He looked at my blade.

**"The bearer of Chaos will come."**

**"I know."**

**"And when he comes..."**

He looked at me.

**"...you'll have to be ready for anything."**

**"Like in—"**

**"Anything."**

I didn't hesitate.

**"Fine."**

Kael nodded.

He vanished.

That night I slept badly.

Not because I was scared.

Because I'd said yes too fast.
And even I knew it was too fast.

choices.text: You refused to think about it.

ikar_comprend_tout.title: What It Meant
ikar_comprend_tout.text:
Yes.

Fire doesn't lie.

*Anything* meant anything.

If Chaos couldn't be controlled —
stop it.

Even if it cost everything.

I was ten.
I had said yes to killing someone if it was necessary.

That thought stayed.

It never left me.

Years later,
when I heard Taera say
*"there's always another way,"*
I thought:
*maybe.*

*But what if there isn't?*

ikar_refuse_penser.title: Not Thinking About It
ikar_refuse_penser.text:
Fire doesn't like an empty head.

So I filled it.

Training.
Combat.
Technique.
Mastery.

I became better than anyone with a blade.

Aryn says I train to run from something.

**"I train to be ready."**

**"Ready for what, exactly?"**

I didn't answer.

She already knew.

We both knew.

We never really talked about it.

ikar_annees.title: The Years
ikar_annees.location: Temple of the Order — Various seasons
ikar_annees.narrator: Ten years old. Eleven. Twelve. Thirteen.
ikar_annees.text:
We grew up.

I was the best at combat.

Taera knew it. She fought differently — defense, protection.
Aryn knew it. She dodged better than she attacked.
Vael knew it. He vanished rather than hold his ground.

Me, I attacked.

Kael used to say:

**"Fire moves forward."**
**"It never backs down."**

I moved forward.

Once Taera stopped me after training.

**"You train to kill."**

**"I train to win."**

**"It's the same thing."**

**"No."**

She left without answering.

I thought about that for a long time.

ikar_taera_raison.title: Taera and the Fight
ikar_taera_raison.text:
Maybe.

Fire that moves forward destroys everything in its path.

Even what it never meant to destroy.

I tried to tell her later.

**"Maybe you were right."**

She looked at me.

**"'Maybe' is a big word coming from you."**

**"Shut up."**

She laughed.

It was rare for me to tell her she was right.

She savored it.

After that we started training differently.
She taught me to protect.
I taught her to strike when it was necessary.

Best decision we ever made.

ikar_nuit_doute.title: The Night of Doubt
ikar_nuit_doute.location: Temple of the Order — His room
ikar_nuit_doute.text:
I was fifteen.

One night, Kael came back.

Without warning.
The way they do.

He looked at me.

**"You doubt."**

**"No."**

**"Don't lie to fire."**

A long silence.

**"What if we can save him?"** I said.
**"What if Aryn is right?"**
**"What if there's another way?"**

Kael said nothing.

**"Answer me."**

**"A fire that hesitates goes out."**

**"That's not an answer."**

He vanished.

It was the last time he spoke to me directly.

choices.text: He never spoke to you again?

ikar_silence_kael.title: Kael's Silence
ikar_silence_kael.text:
Four years of silence.

He was still there.
I could feel him.

But no more words.

I understood later that this was his answer.

*If you have to ask the question, you already know the answer.*

Kael only spoke to those who needed to hear.

I needed to find it on my own.

Four years of searching.

I didn't find it.

But I learned to live with uncertainty.

Maybe that was the real lesson.

ikar_veille.title: The Signal
ikar_veille.location: Temple of the Order — Ikar's room
ikar_veille.text:
I sensed the Chaos before anyone else.

Not because I was stronger.

Because fire recognizes destruction.

My blade ignited on its own.

The first time in years.

I'd set it on the table.
It was burning for no reason.

I looked at the flame.

For a long time.

Then I stood up.
I put on my armor.

I knocked on Aryn's door.

She was already up.

choices.text: What were you thinking at that moment?

ikar_pensee_veille.title: What He Was Thinking
ikar_pensee_veille.text:
The same thing as for the past ten years.

*Ready for anything.*

And for the first time in ten years
I hoped it wouldn't go that far.

Not for me.

For them.

Aryn, who had always been looking for another way.
Taera, who refused to admit there might not be one.
Vael, who pretended not to think about it.

If I was the only one who was right —

That meant I'd have to do something
none of them could do.

Alone.

I hoped I was wrong.

ikar_depart.title: The Departure
ikar_depart.text:
There were four of us in the courtyard.

Vael was whistling.

**"Stop."** I said.

**"Why?"**

**"Because."**

**"Solid argument."**

He stopped anyway.

Taera was gripping her sword.

Aryn was looking west.

Kael appeared one last time.

Right there.
In the air.

He didn't say anything.

But he looked at my blade.

It was burning.

He nodded.

Then he was gone.

**"Let's go."** I said.

ikar_route.title: The Road
ikar_route.text:
I was moving fast.

The others followed.

Aryn said nothing.
She knew what I was thinking.

Taera asked halfway there:

**"What are you going to do when we get there?"**

**"What has to be done."**

**"Ikar."**

**"What has to be done."**

She didn't push.

Vael caught up with me farther on.

He'd stopped whistling.

**"You don't have to carry this alone."**

**"I'm not carrying anything."**

**"Ikar."**

**"What."**

**"You don't have to carry this alone."**

He went back to the rear.

I didn't answer.

But I slowed down a bit.

ikar_fumee.title: The Smoke
ikar_fumee.text:
We saw the smoke from a ridge.

Black.
Thick.

My blade flared up again.

Aryn closed her eyes.

**"He's still there."** she said.

**"Alive?"**

**"Alive."**

Taera murmured something.
A prayer, maybe.

Vael stopped whistling.

I looked at the smoke.

And I thought:

*I hope I'm wrong.*

**"Let's go."** I said.

We rode off at a gallop.

ikar_derniere_pensee.title: The Last Thought
ikar_derniere_pensee.text:
If we could save him —

Aryn would find a way.
Taera would reach out.
Vael would find the right words.

And me.

What would I do?

I'd fight.

But for what, exactly.

Against what, exactly.

For the first time in ten years
I didn't know.

The fire in my blade burned hot.

It didn't know either.

We kept moving anyway.

fin_memoire_ikar.title: Ending — Ikar's Memory
fin_memoire_ikar.text:
The memory goes out.

Like a flame no one blows out, one that simply burns itself out.

ikar_feu_obeit.title: Obedience
ikar_feu_obeit.text:
Not always.

At first it did whatever it wanted.

But quickly.

Much faster than the others with their elements.

Aryn took months to control water.

Fire obeyed me in weeks.

Kael said it was because fire and I
understood each other naturally.

Same intention.
Same impatience.
Same way of moving forward without looking back.

We were alike.

I don't know if that's reassuring or disturbing.

ikar_pere_manque.title: The Forge
ikar_pere_manque.text:
Yes.

Not in a dramatic way.

Just small things.

The smell of hot metal.
The sound of the hammer.
The silence that meant something.

There was no forge in Aurenthal.

The first few months I went down to the Temple kitchens.
Just to hear the fire in the ovens.

Taera asked me what I was doing there.

**"Nothing."**

She nodded.

She understood without my having to explain.

That's one of the things I love about her.

She doesn't make people talk.

ikar_isole.title: Isolation
ikar_isole.text:
Yes.

When you decide fast and the others hesitate —
you often end up alone at the front.

At the forge, after the accident,
the village kids stopped playing with me.

Not out of meanness.
Out of fear.

I understood them.

A kid who can set things on fire without meaning to —
that's not the kind of friend you pick.

I learned to do without the others.

Later, in the Order, I learned that was a mistake.

Needing others isn't a weakness.

Thinking you can carry everything alone is a mistake.

Vael told me that once.

I heard it.
Three years after he'd said it.

ikar_vael_taera_debut.title: Vael and Taera
ikar_vael_taera_debut.location: Temple of the Order — First days
ikar_vael_taera_debut.text:
Taera was easy.

She smiled at everyone.
She really listened to you.
She did what needed doing without being asked.

The first week she brought me bread.

**"You didn't eat this morning."**

**"How do you know?"**

**"I looked."**

Just like that.

Vael was different.

He smiled too, but for the wrong reasons.

To unsettle people.
To test them.
To see how they reacted.

The third week he made my blade vanish during training.

**"Very funny."**

**"I wanted to see if you'd panic."**

**"And?"**

**"You just scorched the floor."**
**"As far as panic goes, that's reasonable."**

We ended up laughing.

That surprised me.

ikar_kael_autres.title: What Kael Thought
ikar_kael_autres.text:
Once.

Just once.

**"The other spirits are different from me."**

**"Better?"**

**"Different."**

**"Water searches."**
**"Earth endures."**
**"Air goes around."**

**"And fire?"**

**"Moves forward."**

**"Is that all?"**

**"It's enough."**

He vanished.

I didn't find that very useful at the time.

Over time I understood.

Each element has its own way of being in the world.

Mine is to move forward.

The others move differently.

That's why there are five of us and not one.

ikar_depart_aryn.title: Aryn's Gaze
ikar_depart_aryn.text:
She was watching me.

She knew what I was thinking.

She had known for ten years.

**"Ikar."**

**"What."**

**"We try first."**

**"I know."**

**"No."** she said.
**"You don't know."**
**"You *promise*."**

I'd never heard her ask me that.

**"I promise to try first."**

She nodded.

A promise to Aryn.

It weighed on me.

ikar_depart_taera.title: Taera's Gaze
ikar_depart_taera.text:
Taera was looking at the sky.

**"What are you thinking about?"** I asked.

It was rare for me to ask questions.

**"The village."**
**"Hers."**
**"What it was like before."**

**"You've never seen her village."**

**"No."**
**"But I imagine it."**
**"Ordinary people."**
**"Who got up in the morning."**

She stopped.

**"That's who we're going for."** she said.
**"Not for the legends."**
**"Not for the Order."**
**"For ordinary people."**

I had forgotten that.

Ten years thinking about the mission.
About technique.
About Chaos.

Not about the people.

ikar_route_promesse.title: The Promise
ikar_route_promesse.text:
*Try first.*

I didn't even know what that meant in practice.

Try what?

Talk?
Aryn would talk better than me.

Reach out?
Taera would do that naturally.

Find the right words?
Vael was born for that.

And me.

If it didn't work out.
If the others couldn't manage it.

That's where I'd step in.

*Try first.*

It meant:
being the last resort.

Not the first.

Maybe that was my place in this group.

Not the front.

The rear guard.
